Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Robert Hooke observed cells in a cork slice with the help of a primitive microscope in the year 1665.
False 1: Robert Hooke observed cells in a cork slice with the help of a primitive microscope in the year 1855.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Robert Hooke called these boxes cells; cell is a Latin word for 'a little room'.
False 1: Robert Brown called these boxes cells; cell is a Latin word for 'a little room'.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Leeuwenhoek (1674), with the improved microscope, discovered free living cells in pond water for the first time.
False 1: Robert Hooke (1674), with the improved microscope, discovered free living cells in pond water for the first time.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Robert Brown in 1831 discovered the nucleus in the cell.
False 1: Leeuwenhoek in 1831 discovered the nucleus in the cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Purkinje in 1839 coined the term 'protoplasm' for the fluid substance of the cell.
False 1: Virchow in 1839 coined the term 'protoplasm' for the fluid substance of the cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The cell theory – that all plants and animals are composed of cells and that the cell is the basic unit of life – was presented by Schleiden (1838) and Schwann (1839).
False 1: The cell theory was presented by Leeuwenhoek (1838) and Hooke (1839).

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The cell theory was further expanded by Virchow (1855) by suggesting that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
False 1: The cell theory was further expanded by Schleiden (1855) by suggesting that all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: With the discovery of the electron microscope in 1940, it was possible to observe and understand the complex structure of the cell and its various organelles.
False 1: With the discovery of the electron microscope in 1665, it was possible to observe and understand the complex structure of the cell and its various organelles.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Organisms whose cells lack a nuclear membrane are called prokaryotes; organisms with cells having a nuclear membrane are called eukaryotes.
False 1: Organisms whose cells lack a nuclear membrane are called eukaryotes; organisms with cells having a nuclear membrane are called prokaryotes.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
False 1: Cells arise spontaneously from non-living matter.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The plasma membrane allows or permits the entry and exit of some materials in and out of the cell; it is called a selectively permeable membrane.
False 1: The plasma membrane allows free entry and exit of all materials in and out of the cell; it is called a freely permeable membrane.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Diffusion is the movement of a substance from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
False 1: Diffusion is the movement of a substance from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane is called osmosis.
False 1: The movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane is called diffusion.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Osmosis is the net diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward a higher solute concentration.
False 1: Osmosis is the net diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward a lower solute concentration.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: If the medium surrounding the cell has a higher water concentration than the cell (hypotonic solution), the cell will gain water by osmosis and swell up.
False 1: If the medium surrounding the cell has a lower water concentration than the cell (hypertonic solution), the cell will gain water by osmosis and swell up.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: If the medium has exactly the same water concentration as the cell (isotonic solution), there will be no net movement of water across the cell membrane.
False 1: If the medium has a higher water concentration than the cell (hypotonic solution), there will be no net movement of water across the cell membrane.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: If the medium has a lower concentration of water than the cell (hypertonic solution), the cell will lose water by osmosis and shrink.
False 1: If the medium has a higher concentration of water than the cell (hypotonic solution), the cell will lose water by osmosis and shrink.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The plasma membrane is flexible and is made up of organic molecules called lipids and proteins.
False 1: The cell wall is flexible and is made up of organic molecules called lipids and proteins.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The flexibility of the cell membrane enables the cell to engulf food and other material from its external environment; this process is known as endocytosis.
False 1: The flexibility of the cell membrane enables the cell to engulf food and other material from its external environment; this process is known as osmosis.
False 2: The flexibility of the cell wall enables the cell to engulf food and other material from its external environment; this process is known as endocytosis.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Amoeba acquires its food through endocytosis.
False 1: Amoeba acquires its food through osmosis.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Plant cells have an additional rigid outer covering called the cell wall, which lies outside the plasma membrane and is mainly composed of cellulose.
False 1: Animal cells have an additional rigid outer covering called the cell wall, which lies outside the plasma membrane.
False 2: The plant cell wall is mainly composed of lipids.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: When a living plant cell loses water through osmosis, the shrinkage of cell contents away from the cell wall is known as plasmolysis.
False 1: When a living plant cell gains water through osmosis, the shrinkage of cell contents away from the cell wall is known as plasmolysis.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Cell walls permit cells of plants, fungi and bacteria to withstand very dilute (hypotonic) external media without bursting.
False 1: The plasma membrane alone permits cells of plants, fungi and bacteria to withstand very dilute (hypotonic) external media without bursting.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The nucleus has a double layered covering called nuclear membrane, which has pores allowing transfer of material from nucleus to cytoplasm.
False 1: The nucleus has a single layered covering called nuclear membrane.
False 2: The nucleus has a double layered covering called plasma membrane.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Chromosomes contain information for inheritance of characters from parents to next generation in the form of DNA molecules.
False 1: Chromosomes contain information for inheritance of characters from parents to next generation in the form of RNA molecules.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and protein.
False 1: Chromosomes are composed of only DNA, with no protein.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Functional segments of DNA are called genes.
False 1: Functional segments of DNA are called chromosomes.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In a cell which is not dividing, DNA is present as chromatin material – visible as an entangled mass of thread-like structures.
False 1: In a cell which is about to divide, DNA is present as chromatin material – visible as an entangled mass of thread-like structures.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Whenever the cell is about to divide, chromatin material gets organised into chromosomes.
False 1: Chromosomes get disorganised into chromatin material whenever the cell is about to divide.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In organisms like bacteria, the nuclear region containing only nucleic acids without a nuclear membrane is called a nucleoid.
False 1: In organisms like bacteria, the nuclear region containing only nucleic acids without a nuclear membrane is called a nucleus.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The cytoplasm is the fluid content inside the plasma membrane and contains many specialised cell organelles.
False 1: The cytoplasm is the fluid content inside the nuclear membrane.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets.
False 1: The Golgi apparatus is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) has particles called ribosomes attached to its surface; smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) does not.
False 1: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) has particles called ribosomes attached to its surface; rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) does not.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Ribosomes are the sites of protein manufacture.
False 1: Lysosomes are the sites of protein manufacture.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The SER helps in the manufacture of fat molecules (lipids) important for cell function.
False 1: The RER helps in the manufacture of fat molecules (lipids) important for cell function.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The process by which proteins and lipids help in building the cell membrane is known as membrane biogenesis.
False 1: The process by which proteins and lipids help in building the cell membrane is known as endocytosis.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In the liver cells of vertebrates, SER plays a crucial role in detoxifying many poisons and drugs.
False 1: In the liver cells of vertebrates, RER plays a crucial role in detoxifying many poisons and drugs.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The Golgi apparatus consists of a system of membrane-bound vesicles (flattened sacs) arranged in stacks called cisterns.
False 1: The endoplasmic reticulum consists of a system of membrane-bound vesicles arranged in stacks called cisterns.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The Golgi apparatus is involved in the storage, modification and packaging of products in vesicles.
False 1: The endoplasmic reticulum is involved in the storage, modification and packaging of products in vesicles.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The Golgi apparatus is also involved in the formation of lysosomes.
False 1: The endoplasmic reticulum is also involved in the formation of lysosomes.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs filled with digestive enzymes that are made by RER.
False 1: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs filled with digestive enzymes that are made by SER.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Lysosomes help to keep the cell clean by digesting foreign material and worn-out cell organelles; they are known as the 'suicide bags' of a cell.
False 1: Mitochondria help to keep the cell clean by digesting foreign material and worn-out cell organelles; they are known as the 'suicide bags' of a cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell.
False 1: Lysosomes are known as the powerhouses of the cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Mitochondria have two membrane coverings; the outer membrane is porous while the inner membrane is deeply folded.
False 1: Mitochondria have a single membrane covering.
False 2: Mitochondria have two membrane coverings; the inner membrane is porous while the outer membrane is deeply folded.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The energy required for various chemical activities is released by mitochondria in the form of ATP (Adenosine triphosphate) molecules.
False 1: The energy required for various chemical activities is released by ribosomes in the form of ATP (Adenosine triphosphate) molecules.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: ATP is known as the energy currency of the cell.
False 1: ADP is known as the energy currency of the cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes; therefore mitochondria are able to make some of their own proteins.
False 1: Lysosomes have their own DNA and ribosomes; therefore lysosomes are able to make some of their own proteins.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Plastids are present only in plant cells.
False 1: Plastids are present in both plant and animal cells.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: There are two types of plastids: chromoplasts (coloured plastids) and leucoplasts (white or colourless plastids).
False 1: There are three types of plastids: chromoplasts, leucoplasts and amyloplasts.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Chromoplasts containing the pigment chlorophyll are known as chloroplasts and are important for photosynthesis.
False 1: Leucoplasts containing the pigment chlorophyll are known as chloroplasts and are important for photosynthesis.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Leucoplasts are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.
False 1: Chloroplasts are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Plastids also have their own DNA and ribosomes, similar to mitochondria.
False 1: Lysosomes also have their own DNA and ribosomes, similar to mitochondria.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Vacuoles are small sized in animal cells while plant cells have very large vacuoles.
False 1: Vacuoles are large sized in animal cells while plant cells have very small vacuoles.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The central vacuole of some plant cells may occupy 50–90% of the cell volume.
False 1: The central vacuole of some plant cells may occupy 5–10% of the cell volume.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In plant cells, vacuoles are full of cell sap and provide turgidity and rigidity to the cell.
False 1: In animal cells, vacuoles are full of cell sap and provide turgidity and rigidity to the cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In Amoeba, the food vacuole contains the food items that the Amoeba has consumed.
False 1: In Amoeba, the central vacuole contains food items that the Amoeba has consumed.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Prokaryotic cells are generally small (1–10 µm) while eukaryotic cells are generally large (5–100 µm).
False 1: Prokaryotic cells are generally large (5–100 µm) while eukaryotic cells are generally small (1–10 µm).

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The chlorophyll in photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria is associated with membranous vesicles but not with plastids.
False 1: The chlorophyll in photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria is associated with plastids but not with membranous vesicles.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: The process of cell division by which most cells divide for growth is called mitosis; each mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.
False 1: The process of cell division by which most cells divide for growth is called meiosis; each mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In mitosis, the daughter cells have the same number of chromosomes as the mother cell.
False 1: In meiosis, the daughter cells have the same number of chromosomes as the mother cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: In meiosis, a cell produces four new cells, and the new cells have only half the number of chromosomes of the mother cell.
False 1: In meiosis, a cell produces two new cells, and the new cells have only half the number of chromosomes of the mother cell.
False 2: In mitosis, a cell produces four new cells with half the number of chromosomes of the mother cell.

Chapter: 9th Ch05 - The Fundamental Unit of Life
True Statement: Absorption of water by plant roots is also an example of osmosis.
False 1: Absorption of water by plant roots is also an example of diffusion.
